chunks: (They are) like Satan who says to man: "Do not believe;" and when he becomes a disbeliever, he says: "I have nothing to do with you. I fear God, the Lord of all the worlds."
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about Satan's relationship with humans after they disbelieve?
ai.summary: In Surah Al-Hashr, this verse employs the simile of Satan to illustrate the deceptive nature of worldly temptations, a concept central to Shia exegesis regarding the 'nafs' and 'shaytan' as dual internal and external guides. It emphasizes that Satan's promise of guidance is transient, as he ultimately disowns believers upon death or judgment, citing his own fear of Allah to justify his separation. This highlights the necessity of steadfastness in faith, as the ultimate accountability lies with God, not the fleeting whispers of the devil.
